# bugs #3481: Internal error for a call with arguments to a function declared without a prototype

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3481/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17158
- Recommended action: Keep open. Choose between full support, together with feature request #450, and an ordinary error message.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

With sdcc r17158 for mcs51 in the default `--std-c11` mode, the program in the ticket stops with
"FATAL Compiler Internal Error" in `SDCCast.c` and the text "Setting of register parameter vs.
other parameter not yet implemented for functions without prototype". The SIGSEGV of the ticket
does not occur. Every call with arguments to a function that is declared without a prototype stops
this way. Calls without arguments compile, and so do calls after a prototype or the definition is
visible.

## Known

The message is a `wassertl (0, ...)` in `processParms` in `src/SDCCast.c`, which r13701 added for
this ticket. r17176 contains the same line. `processParms` promotes the arguments of such a call
and then stops, because the call has no parameter list.

The code generators take the parameter list from the function type at the call. For mcs51,
`aopArg` and `genSend` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` read `FUNC_ARGS`, and `geniCodeParms` needs the list
for the `_f_PARM_n` symbols of functions that are not reentrant. A parameter list that is inferred
from the arguments therefore has to be stored in that type.

K&R-style definitions on mcs51 do not use the calling convention of functions with a prototype.
The assembly for `int kr(a, b) char a; long b; {...}` reads `a` as one byte from `_kr_PARM_1`, and
callers that see `int kr(char, long);` pass it in DPL. `int kr3(a) int a; {...}` reads
`_kr3_PARM_1`, and `int kr2(a) {...}` with an implicit `int` reads DPTR.
`mergeKRDeclListIntoFuncDecl` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` replaces the type of each parameter after
`processFunc` has marked the register parameters in the type that it replaces. Calls through a
declaration without a prototype would disagree with such definitions in other files, and sdcc
would give no diagnostic.

## Open

Full support needs two changes in code that all ports share. The first call has to give the
function a parameter list that is inferred from the arguments after promotion. K&R-style
definitions have to take their parameters after promotion and with the register convention of
functions with a prototype. Every port has to be verified.

The small alternative is an ordinary error message that asks for a prototype, in place of the
internal error. C23 has no function declarators without a prototype.

## Related

Bug #3021 stops with the same internal error. Feature request #450 asks for K&R-style functions.
The test `support/regression/tests/bug-3481.c` from r13701 has its body inside `#if 0`.
